responsibility: This module provides GCC’s core infrastructure containers and memory-management utilities that are reused across front ends, middle-end analyses, and target code. It covers the compiler’s generic allocation mechanisms—fixed-size object pools, obstack helpers, and the GGC garbage-collected allocator with both full page-based and no-GC backends—along with the shared root-marking, PCH, accounting, and selftest support that let compiler objects be allocated, preserved, and reclaimed safely. It also defines the standard reusable data structures that many passes depend on: sparse bitmaps for dataflow-style integer sets, vec for dynamic arrays, hash_table/hash_map/hash_set and their trait adapters for typed hashed storage, Fibonacci heaps and splay-tree variants for priority-queue and ordered-map behavior, plus vector-building and vector-permutation index helpers used to represent compact vector constants and permutation masks. Overall, this module is the compiler’s low-level container and allocator substrate rather than a language-specific or optimization-specific subsystem.
